propositions.text: The claimant is a 26-year-old Mexican citizen who arrived in Canada on April 11, 2008 and sought refugee protection four days later.
propositions.quote: The claimant, XXXX XXXXXXX XXXXXX, is a citizen of Mexico. He is twenty-six (26) years old. The claimant arrived in Canada on April 11, 2008, and four days later, asked for refugee protection in Canada pursuant to section 96 of the Immigration and Refugee Protection Act (the Act)

propositions.text: The claimant alleges a well-founded fear of persecution due to membership in a particular social group under section 96 of the Act.
propositions.quote: alleging a well-founded fear of persecution as a result of his membership in a particular social group

propositions.text: The claimant requests protection under section 97(1) as a person at risk of life or cruel treatment if removed to Mexico.
propositions.quote: The claimant is also requesting Canada's protection pursuant to section 97(1) of the Act as a person whose removal to his country of nationality would subject him personally to a risk to his life or to a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment and torture

propositions.text: The hearing was originally scheduled for January 6, 2011 but did not proceed due to technical difficulties with video conference.
propositions.quote: The Tribunal notes that this hearing was originally convoked for January 6, 2011, but did not proceed due to technical difficulties with the video conference

paragraphs.summary: The court states the claimant is a 26-year-old Mexican who sought refugee protection in Canada under sections 96 and 97(1) of the Act; hearing was delayed by technical issues.

propositions.text: The claimant alleged he and a friend were victims of a car-jacking and recognized one car-jacker from school.
propositions.quote: the claimant alleged that he and a friend, XXXX XXXX, had been the victims of a car-jacking. The claimant alleged that he had recognized one of the car-jackers, XXXX XXXX, from his school

propositions.text: The claimant alleged he never saw his friend again and was threatened by the car-jacker.
propositions.quote: Subsequent to the event, the claimant never saw his friend XXXX again and was threatened by the car-jacker, XXXX XXXX

paragraphs.summary: The claimant alleges he and a friend were car-jacking victims; he recognized a car-jacker and was threatened, and never saw his friend again.

propositions.text: The Tribunal concludes the claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection for reasons given below.
propositions.quote: The Tribunal concludes that the claimant is neither a "Convention refugee" nor a "person in need of protection" for the reasons given below

paragraphs.summary: The Tribunal concludes the claimant is neither a Convention refugee nor a person in need of protection.

propositions.text: The Tribunal does not accept the claimant's identity.
propositions.quote: The Tribunal does not accept the claimant's identity

paragraphs.summary: The Tribunal does not accept the claimant's identity.

propositions.text: The claimant produced a Mexican passport issued in 2008 but no other identity documents.
propositions.quote: To support his identity, the claimant produced a passport from Mexico which was issued XXXX, 2008. He did not produce any corroborating evidence of his identity such as a birth certificate, an electoral card or any other identification

propositions.text: The claimant changed address dates in his testimony, conflicting with passport issuance date.
propositions.quote: At the claimant's first hearing, which did not proceed, he made some changes to the dates where he lived at certain addresses in Mexico... However, the claimant's passport shows that he was issued a passport in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX on XXXX, 2008 - three days after he was supposed to be living in hiding in Mexico City

propositions.text: The Tribunal finds the claimant's explanation for having his birth certificate while in hiding not credible.
propositions.quote: The Tribunal does not find this to be a credible explanation and finds that the claimant has not met the burden of establishing his identity

paragraphs.summary: The Tribunal finds discrepancies in the claimant's identity documents and explanations, and does not find his identity credible.

propositions.text: Key issues are claimant's credibility and Internal Flight Alternative; identity became an issue during hearing.
propositions.quote: The key issues explored at the hearing were the claimant's credibility and an Internal Flight Alternative (IFA). Identity became an issue during the hearing when the claimant was unable to answer questions about how he had obtained his passport

paragraphs.summary: The Tribunal identifies credibility and Internal Flight Alternative as key issues; identity was questioned during hearing.

propositions.text: No documents were filed to support the claim; claimant could not explain implausible story parts or additions at hearing.
propositions.quote: No documents were filed in support of this claim. The claimant was unable to expand upon or explain implausible sections of the story in his PIF. The claimant was unable to explain why he added significant elements to his story at the hearing that he had not included in his PIF

propositions.text: The Tribunal found the claimant not credible about his identity or alleged experience in Mexico.
propositions.quote: The Tribunal found that the claimant was not credible either about his identity or his alleged experience in Mexico

paragraphs.summary: The Tribunal found the claimant not credible and no supporting documents were filed; claimant could not explain story inconsistencies.

propositions.text: Claimant's counsel advised claim was solely under Section 97(1)(b) of the Act, not Section 96.
propositions.quote: Counsel for the claimant advised the Tribunal that this claim was made solely under Section 97 (1) b of the Act. There was no evidence presented at the hearing which indicated any basis for a claim under Section 96 of the Act

propositions.text: The claim will be analyzed under Section 97(1)(b) of the Act.
propositions.quote: This claim will be analyzed as a claim under Section 97 (1) b of the Act

paragraphs.summary: The claim is analyzed solely under Section 97(1)(b) as claimant's counsel confirmed no basis under Section 96.

propositions.text: Claimant's testimony differed from PIF on three critical points: friend's fate, claimant's actions after car-jacking, and consequences on claimant's parents.
propositions.quote: The claimant's testimony differed from the statements in his PIF on three critical points: a) What happened to his friend XXXX after the car-jacking? b) Where the claimant went and what he did after the car-jacking? c) The consequences of the car-jacking on the claimant's parents

paragraphs.summary: The claimant's testimony conflicted with his PIF on three critical points regarding friend, actions after car-jacking, and parents' consequences.

propositions.text: Claimant testified about car-jacking event and that he never saw friend again, who was allegedly assassinated.
propositions.quote: The claimant stated that XXXX was a very good friend of his... He stated in his PIF, at paragraph 8, that XXXX had been assassinated by XXXX XXXX

propositions.text: Tribunal finds claimant's behavior inconsistent with someone experiencing a terrifying assault with a close friend.
propositions.quote: The Tribunal does not find that this reply explains the claimant's behaviour... The Tribunal finds that all of the behaviour described above is not consistent with the behaviour of someone who has experienced a terrifying assault with a close friend

propositions.text: No proof that friend existed, owned car, or that parents were concerned; Tribunal does not believe car-jacking or friend's death occurred.
propositions.quote: There was no proof that XXXX existed, that his family owned a XXXX, or that his parents had any concern about his whereabouts. The Tribunal does not believe that the car-jacking took place as described or that XXXX was killed

paragraphs.summary: The claimant testified about the car-jacking and friend's death, but the Tribunal finds his behavior and evidence not credible.

propositions.text: Claimant said he did not report car-jacking due to fear, moved to grandmother's town, and tried to report crime later but police refused complaint.
propositions.quote: The claimant stated that he went to work the next day and the day after... he decided to move to XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX... he decided to report the crime to the Public Ministry in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX. The claimant stated that the police would not accept his complaint because he had no proof

propositions.text: Tribunal finds it not credible that claimant would attempt to report event two months later without corroboration or proof.
propositions.quote: It is not credible that two months later, the claimant would attempt to denounce an event that took place in another city

propositions.text: Claimant's testimony about seeing aggressor asking for him is inconsistent with PIF and not credible.
propositions.quote: He was questioned how he knew XXXX XXXX was in XXXX XXXX XXXX XXXX because of him... He did not mention in testimony that he knew that XXXX XXXX was making enquiries about him

paragraphs.summary: Claimant's story about reporting crime and seeing aggressors is inconsistent and not credible to the Tribunal.

propositions.text: Claimant alleges parents received threatening calls and were selling house due to threats, but did not include this in PIF.
propositions.quote: He added that 'someone' had been making threatening calls to his parents 'constantly'... his parents were in the process of selling their house because of the constant threats. None of this information was in the PIF

propositions.text: Tribunal does not accept claimant's explanation for omission and does not believe parents received threats.
propositions.quote: The Tribunal does not accept the claimant's explanation for the omission as these are significant allegations. The Tribunal does not believe that the claimant's parents received any threatening calls

paragraphs.summary: Claimant alleges parents received threats and are selling house, but Tribunal rejects explanation and does not believe threats occurred.

propositions.text: Claimant has not established on balance of probabilities that he would face risk to life or cruel treatment if returned to Mexico.
propositions.quote: The Tribunal finds that the claimant has not established, on a balance of probabilities, that it is more probable than not that he would suffer a risk to his life or cruel and unusual treatment or punishment or torture, if he were to return to Mexico

paragraphs.summary: The Tribunal concludes claimant has not proven risk to life or cruel treatment if returned to Mexico.

propositions.text: Claimant has not established it is more likely than not he would face risk to life or cruel treatment under Section 97(1)(a) or (b) if returned to Mexico.
propositions.quote: the Tribunal concludes that the claimant has not established, on the balance of probabilities, that, if he were to return to Mexico, it is more likely than not that he would be subject to a risk to his life, or to a risk of cruel and unusual treatment or punishment or danger of torture pursuant to Section 97(1) (a) or (b) of the Act

paragraphs.summary: The Tribunal concludes claimant has not established risk under Section 97(1)(a) or (b) if returned to Mexico.

propositions.text: Claim for refugee protection is denied.
propositions.quote: Consequently, the claim for refugee protection by XXXX XXXX XXXX is denied

paragraphs.summary: The Tribunal denies the claimant's refugee protection claim.
